_comment: SHOSMED LF3 chemistry review, BATCH 8. Implemented 18 November 2026 from
SHOSMED_LF3_Chemistry_Batch8_Review.txt.
HOW THE IDS WERE VERIFIED. The review supplied ORIGINAL IDENTIFICATION
SIGNATURES (each item's original stem plus all four original option texts),
so the map below was derived by FULL CONTENT MATCH rather than inferred:
1. Each signature was matched against all 485 chemistry records on a
canonical form that decodes entities, strips tags, folds HTML and
Unicode sub/superscripts to plain digits, normalises dashes, quotes,
Greek letters, fractions and arrows, and collapses whitespace. All 60
signatures matched EXACTLY ONE record each.
2. No two of the 485 chemistry records share a full signature, and no two
share even a canonical stem, so no match was ambiguous and none had to
be resolved by topic or answer-letter pattern.
3. Every stored answer letter agreed with the review letter for that
display number, reproducing the review key block and its
A=13/B=16/C=18/D=13 tally. This INCLUDES Q59 and Q60, whose letters the
review determined scientifically because the export exposed no answer
heading: the stored keys are C and A, exactly as the review expects, so
no key was changed and none had to be reported as disagreeing.
4. The four repeats the review asserts were confirmed independently rather
than taken on trust: Q1=chem-369, Q2=chem-382, Q3=chem-396 and
Q4=chem-409 are the content matches, and all four are owned by batch 7
(its Q8, Q21, Q35 and Q48). They are left byte-identical and are NOT
counted again toward coverage.
Contiguity is a RESULT of that verification, not an assumption, and this pack
is NOT contiguous: the 56 new ids run chem-422 .. chem-477, while the four
repeats sit at chem-369, chem-382, chem-396 and chem-409.
THINGS THE REVIEW ASKED TO CHECK RATHER THAN ASSUME:
- Q59 and Q60 genuinely lack their structure IN STORAGE, not merely in the
export. Both stored explanations are bare prose with no markup at all: no
keyed heading, no 'Why the other choices are wrong' heading and no
distractor paragraphs. Nothing was duplicated; each explanation was
rebuilt once, with an unlettered keyed heading matching the surrounding
items and exactly three distractor paragraphs, taking the pack from 174
to the complete 180. Neither gained a point block, Bottom Line or table.
- Q7's and Q8's exponents are ALREADY real exponents in the stored fields:
the records hold "2<sup>n</sup>" and the Unicode superscripts 2², 2³ and
2⁴. The flattened "2n" appearance in the review source is a plain-text
extraction artifact, so nothing was changed there.
- Q53's powers of ten are ALREADY real exponents: the record holds eleven
<sup> elements, including "1.8 x 10<sup>-5</sup>" and "x<sup>2</sup>".
Another extraction artifact; the markup was left alone.
- Q55's option texts are intact and were NOT changed. Its line-broken
appearance in the export comes from <sub> markup inside the options.
Its charge notations, however, were a genuine stored defect: the record
held "C2<sup>2</sup>-", "C<sup>4</sup>-" and "[:C≡C:]<sup>2</sup>-",
which render with an unsubscripted 2 and the sign outside the exponent.
The review asks for these to be rendered unambiguously, so they are now
C₂²⁻, C⁴⁻ and [:C≡C:]²⁻.
PRESENTATION DECISIONS, recorded rather than silently applied:
- Dash characters in the review's replacement prose were normalised to the
character the SAME item already uses for the SAME token, per the review's
rule that existing punctuation conventions be matched without a bank-wide
cleanup. Q13 'H-H/Cl-Cl/H-Cl' use U+2212 as its stem does; Q26 '200-250',
Q30 'C-C' and Q35 '30-32' use the ASCII hyphen each item already uses;
Q41's new stem and feedback use the ASCII hyphen-minus of its retained
calculation. Q24's 'X–X' had no in-item precedent and keeps the review's
en dash, which the bank already uses for bond dashes elsewhere.
- Chemical sub/superscripts supplied by the review were kept as supplied and
never downgraded. Q52's and Q50's replaced passages therefore use proper
subscripts while their retained option texts keep the older flattened
forms; a whole-item notation cleanup was out of scope.
- Q53's replaced passages use <sup> exponents and the item's ASCII
hyphen-minus so they read consistently with the retained calculation
steps around them, while using proper subscripts as the review requires.
- Synchronized headings reproduce their option text exactly, so that
heading-equals-option is machine-checkable. Option texts other than the
eleven the review names were not touched, so no further 'formatting
normalization' was applied to a heading.

Structural and consistency checks establish scope and presentation. They do not establish scientific accuracy, which rests on the content review itself.

items.change: The muscle nitrogen-export routes are given explicitly: alanine by transamination of pyruvate, glutamine by glutamine synthetase at an ATP cost.
items.from: Skeletal muscle does not have a complete urea cycle. Instead, muscle disposes of amino group nitrogen by transamination to form alanine (glucose-alanine cycle) or glutamine, which are transported to the liver for urea synthesis.
items.to: Skeletal muscle does not have a complete urea cycle. It exports nitrogen mainly as alanine and glutamine. Alanine is formed by transamination of pyruvate; glutamine is formed from glutamate and ammonia by glutamine synthetase in a reaction that uses ATP. These molecules carry nitrogen to other organs, including the liver, where it can be converted to urea.
